subject: social_science

concepts.title: Diverse Developmental Aspirations
concepts.definition: The principle that different individuals or groups possess unique and sometimes clashing objectives for progress based on their specific life conditions.
concepts.key_idea: Progress is subjective and varies across different social and economic categories.
question_patterns: Why do different people have different goals for development?
Explain how developmental goals can be conflicting with an example.
What might be progress for a landless labourer?
How do aspirations of a rich urban girl differ from her brother?
Can development for one be destructive for another?
Identify the developmental goals of a prosperous farmer.

solution_steps.explain: Determine the social or economic background of the individual or group mentioned.
Evaluate the specific requirements and desires relevant to that person's life situation.
Check if these goals conflict with the interests of other groups, such as industrialists versus tribals.

concepts.title: Non-Material Developmental Goals
concepts.definition: Aspects of life that contribute to well-being but cannot be purchased with money, such as liberty, safety, and social standing.
concepts.key_idea: Quality of life depends on both financial resources and intangible social factors.
question_patterns: What are the goals people seek besides higher income?
Why is equal treatment considered a developmental goal?
How does job security affect a person's choice of employment?
Explain the importance of non-material factors in development.
Give examples of things that cannot be measured but are important for life.
How does the dignity of women in society relate to development?

solution_steps.explain: Identify material factors like wages and non-material factors like freedom or respect.
Analyze how individuals might choose lower pay for better security or working conditions.

concepts.title: Per Capita Income
concepts.section: How to Compare Different Countries or States?
concepts.definition: A measure of the average earnings per person in a nation, found by dividing the total national earnings by the total number of inhabitants.
concepts.key_idea: Average income serves as a standard tool for comparing the economic level of different regions.
question_patterns: What is per capita income?
How is the average income of a country calculated?
Calculate the per capita income if the total income is {total_income} and population is {total_population}.
What is the other name for average income?
Why is total income not a suitable measure for comparing countries?
Find the average income for a group of people.

solution_steps.explain: Obtain the sum of all incomes of the residents in the country.
Determine the total number of people living in the country.
Divide the total income by the population to find the average.

concepts.title: World Bank Country Classification
concepts.section: How to Compare Different Countries or States?
concepts.definition: The categorization of nations into high, middle, or low income groups based on specific per capita income thresholds defined by the World Bank.
concepts.key_idea: Economic classification of countries depends on annual US dollar income benchmarks.
question_patterns: What criterion does the World Bank use to classify countries?
Define a high-income country according to the World Development Report.
What is the income threshold for low-income countries in 2024?
In which category does India fall based on its per capita income?
What are the limitations of using only average income for comparison?
How does the World Bank distinguish between developed and underdeveloped nations?

solution_steps.explain: Compare the country's per capita income with the World Bank's set limits.
Classify as rich if above 66500 USD or low-income if below 2300 USD.

concepts.title: Infant Mortality Rate
concepts.definition: The count of infants who pass away before reaching their first birthday for every one thousand live births in a specific year.
concepts.key_idea: IMR reflects the quality of healthcare and nutritional support available to infants.
question_patterns: Define Infant Mortality Rate.
What does a high IMR indicate about a state's development?
Compare the IMR of Kerala and Haryana.
Why is IMR considered an important indicator of development?
How many children die before age one per 1000 births in Kerala?
What is the significance of the year 2020 data in the context of IMR?

solution_steps.explain: Find the number of children dying before age one.
Express this number relative to 1000 live births.

concepts.title: Literacy Rate
concepts.definition: The percentage of the population aged seven years and older who are able to read and write.
concepts.key_idea: Literacy measures the basic educational attainment of a society.
question_patterns: What is the definition of literacy rate?
How is the literacy rate of a region measured?
Which age group is considered for calculating literacy rate?
Compare the literacy rates of Bihar and Kerala.
What percentage of the population in Haryana is literate?
Why is literacy rate a better indicator than just income?

solution_steps.explain: Identify the population that is 7 years old or older.
Find the ratio of literate individuals to the filtered population.

concepts.title: Public Facilities and Collective Provision
concepts.definition: Services and goods, such as schools and healthcare, provided by the government or community because they are more affordable and efficient when shared.
concepts.key_idea: Individual wealth cannot always buy essential services like a clean environment or disease protection.
question_patterns: Why are public facilities necessary for development?
Give examples of goods provided collectively.
How does the Public Distribution System (PDS) help in development?
Why can't money buy a pollution-free environment?
Explain the role of government in providing education.
Why is collective security cheaper than individual security?

solution_steps.explain: Identify a service needed by the community (e.g., sanitation).
Compare the cost of providing it to one person versus the whole community.

concepts.title: Body Mass Index
concepts.definition: A numerical value derived from the mass and height of a person to determine if they are undernourished, normal, or overweight.
concepts.key_idea: BMI is a standard tool used by nutritionists to evaluate physical health based on body proportions.
question_patterns: How do you calculate Body Mass Index (BMI)?
What is the BMI of a person weighing {weight} kg and {height} meters tall?
What does a BMI of less than 18.5 indicate?
Calculate the BMI for a student with weight {weight} and height {height}.
Why do scientists use BMI to measure nourishment?
What is the formula for BMI?

solution_steps.explain: Multiply the height in meters by itself.
Divide the weight in kilograms by the squared height.

concepts.title: Human Development Index
concepts.definition: A composite statistic produced by the UNDP that ranks countries based on health, education, and per capita income levels.
concepts.key_idea: HDI provides a broader view of development than income alone by including life expectancy and schooling.
question_patterns: What does HDI stand for?
Which organization publishes the Human Development Report?
What are the three main indicators used in HDI?
Compare India's HDI rank with Sri Lanka's.
Define life expectancy at birth.
Why is HDI a more comprehensive measure of development?

solution_steps.explain: Collect data on GNI per capita, life expectancy, and mean years of schooling.
Compare the aggregate score against other nations to determine the rank.

concepts.title: Sustainability of Development
concepts.definition: The practice of developing in a way that meets current needs without compromising the ability of future generations to meet theirs.
concepts.key_idea: Resources must be managed carefully to prevent exhaustion and environmental decay.
question_patterns: What is sustainable development?
Why is the overuse of groundwater a concern for sustainability?
Distinguish between renewable and non-renewable resources.
How long will the world's crude oil reserves last at current extraction rates?
Why do environmental consequences not respect national boundaries?
Explain the quote regarding inheriting the world from forefathers.

solution_steps.explain: Determine if the resource is renewable (like water) or non-renewable (like oil).
Compare the rate of extraction or use with the rate of natural replenishment.

solution_template.explain: The total income is given as {total_income}.

worked_examples.question_pattern: If the average income of 4 families is {avg_inc}, what is the total income of all families?

solution_template.explain: Average = Total / Population, so Total = Average * Population.
